Chronicling the buildup to the global tournament taking place in the United States, Mexico and Canada, 2025-26 Panini Select Road to FIFA World Cup 2026 Soccer highlights national team stars in contention for qualification.

Hobby boxes ($499.95) average three autographs or relics, along with multiple parallels and inserts. There's also the 1st Off the Line (FOTL) format with exclusive content.

This release joins other Road to World Cup sets from Donruss, National Treasures and Noir.

The card designs match the club-based La Liga and Ligue 1 editions.

Base Set (Japanese: 拡張パック Expansion Pack) is the name given to the first main expansion of cards of the Pokémon Trading Card Game. The set is the first to feature all 151 Generation I Pokémon in the card game.

Blurb

Put the power in your hand with the Pokémon trading card game!

The hugely successful Pokémon Game Boy® game was just the beginning of the Pokémon phenomenon. Now, with the trad
[…]
Base Set is the name given to the first main expansion of the Pokémon Trading Card Game. In Japan, it was released as a starter deck (Starter Pack, スターターパック) alongside separately purchasable Base Set packs (Expansion Pack, 拡張パック)[1][2]. The Base Set was promoted through the giveaway of the first TCG cards, a Pikachu and Jigglypuff promo that were peeled from a CoroCoro magazine 5 days ahead of the main release. The promos were advertised to be collected alongside the main set, making CoroCoro readers feel that they had already started the collection[2]. The Base Set is based on Pokémon Red, Blue, and Green, featuring Generation I Pokémon. The English expansion was released on January 9, 1999, while the Japanese expansion was released on October 20, 1996.

The English release are ordered by card type (Pokémon, Trainer, and Energy cards), then by rarity (Rare Holo, Rare, Uncommon, Common), lastly, alphabetically by card name. The Japanese release are ordered by the types first, then ascending rarity (Rare and Rare Holo are considered the same), then National Pokédex number, followed by Trainer and Energy cards.

references.title: Top Pelé Cards of All-Time, Best Rookies List, Autographs, Guide
references.text:
Top Pelé Cards of All-Time, Best Rookies List, Autographs, Guide

When you click on links to various merchants on this site and make a purchase, this can result in this site earning a commission. Affiliate programs and affiliations include, but are not limited to, the eBay Partner Network.

Home » Soccer » Soccer Cards » Top Pelé Cards to Collect

Tweet
Share
Pin10
Share
Email
10 Shares

The greatest soccer player in history was born Edson Arantes do Nascimento, but everyone else knows him as Pelé. Despite not appearing on the pitch in many decades, Pelé enjoys a near-mythical reputation as the best player in the most popular sport in the world. Thanks to his lasting legacy and inclusion in modern sets, Pelé cards and autographs remain at the forefront of the hobby and many of the key Pelé cards are in high demand.

The Brazilian-born Pel
[…]
While it is hard to definitively name one Pelé card as his true rookie card, the 1958 Alifabolaget card released in Sweden is arguably the best of the bunch. Several regional cards with low production lay claim to the Pele rookie card title, so it really just boils down to personal preference, budget and card availability. With a full-color image and appealing look, the Alifabolaget is a great card, if you can find one.

1958 Colecao Titulares Pelé #50, #86
Buy on eBay.
Released the same year, the Brazilian Titulares set features a few key rookie options, as well. Top choices include card #50 with a background action shot, along with the #86 card, which features a better image of the global icon. There is also a Selecao Brasileira team card with Pelé (#88).

1958 Swedish Rekord Journal Pele
Buy on eBay.
This early Pelé card remains popular despite oddball origins. The dual "card" is actually cut from a Swedish magazine and normally includes Manoel Francisco Santos, although some are cut further to present the Pelé card solo. Due to its thin magazine stock and the fact that it is literally cut from a magazine, this is generally considered the least preferred of the options vying for rookie card status.
One interesting note is that this card appears to feature Pelé's full name. However, upon closer examination, the card is attributed to "Edvaldo Alves Santarosa." Edvaldo Alves de Santa Rosa is actually the official name for the original Dida, a former Brazilian soccer star, who passed away in 2002.

1958-59 Tupinamba Ltda. Quigol Pelé #109

Jump to the 2018-19 Panini Prizm Mosaic Basketball checklist and team set lists.

Like the previous year’s release, 2018-19 Panini Prizm Mosaic Basketball is an online-exclusive set available through the company’s website.

Offering an abbreviated checklist over the core 2018-19 Panini Prizm Basketball set, each three-pack box has nine parallels.

The base set has just 100 cards. That means top stars and key rookies from the season. Rather than the regular Opti-Chrome background Prizm cards have, these all have a shiny pattern background that reflects to look almost like diamonds.

Parallels take the color route, similar to Panini’s other chromium releases. Gold (/10) and Black (1/1) are among the hardest to pull.

Autographs come with on-card signatures. Limited to just over 30 players, the checklist of signers includes Luka Doncic, Trae Young, Shaquille O’Neal, Charles Barkley, Stephen Curry and Giannis Antetokounmpo. These are not in every box.

Boxes of 2018-19 Panini Prizm Mosaic Basketball can be purchased here.
